mainTopic: An animal bought from a non-Jew: רבי ישמעאל's age limits for a definite בכור, רבי יהושע's and רבי עקיבא's responses, and the גמרא's analysis of טינוף and זעירי's thirty-day rule.
overview: The amud opens by settling an earlier question. רבי ישמעאל takes a מיעוט (minority) into account, like רבי מאיר. רבינא offers another approach: even רבנן do not rely on a רוב that depends on an action, such as mating. A ברייתא then gives רבי ישמעאל's age limits for when the next male of an animal bought from a non-Jew is a definite בכור, with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה giving a donkey an extra year. רבי יהושע says רבי ישמעאל erred, because signs like a טינוף (murky discharge) or a שליא also exempt the mother, and a young goat can have a טינוף and still give birth within its year. רבי עקיבא rejects using age at all: only known facts decide, and a ספק בכור is eaten by the owner once it has a מום. The גמרא explains the first dispute as whether we worry about an unseen טינוף, or alternatively whether an animal that had a טינוף can still give birth within its first year. It then asks how רבי יהושע's received tradition differs from his own reasoning. It answers that they differ over זעירי's thirty-day rule, or alternatively that both accept זעירי and argue about birth after incomplete months, an explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority, like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר, who is חושש למיעוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is clear that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes an earlier discussion and settles on an answer: רבי ישמעאל's rule follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל says that once a goat is past its first year, its next offspring is only a ספק בכור. He says this even though most goats that age have already given birth. That means he takes the minority that have not yet given birth seriously, which is exactly רבי מאיר's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear; the plain conclusion after other attempts failed

steps.whyThisMatters: It connects רבי ישמעאל's practical rule about animals to a basic dispute about how far we may rely on a רוב.

phrases.english: It is clear
phrases.notes: Signals the conclusion after earlier suggestions.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds like Rabbi Meir,
who is concerned for the minority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion from the previous part of the daf about which תנא רבי ישמעאל follows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר and takes the minority into account.

steps.title: רבינא: even רבנן would agree here
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רבנן follow a majority only when it does not depend on an action. Giving birth depends on mating, so even רבנן would not rely on that majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: You can even say רבי ישמעאל follows רבנן. רבנן follow the majority only when the majority does not depend on an action. A majority that depends on an action, they do not follow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a second explanation, so רבי ישמעאל need not follow רבי מאיר against רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some majorities are simply how nature works. Others depend on something happening, and an animal giving birth depends on whether it mated. רבנן trust only the first kind, so רבי ישמעאל's caution fits their view too.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying רבנן ignore the רוב in general. He is pointing out an exception: a majority that depends on some action happening is not the kind they rely on.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general principle about which kinds of majority count in הלכה.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
You may even say it is the Rabbis,
when the Rabbis follow the majority,
it is a majority that does not depend on an action,
but a majority that depends on an action, they do not follow.
phrases.notes: Giving birth depends on mating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the conclusion that רבי ישמעאל follows only רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל must disagree with רבנן, who follow the רוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן do not rely on a majority that depends on an action, so רבי ישמעאל can agree with them.

steps.title: Age limits for a certain firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the ages up to which an animal's next offspring is surely a בכור: a goat in its first year, a ewe in its second, a cow in its third. A donkey follows the rule of a cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A goat in its first year: the offspring certainly goes to the כהן. After that, it is uncertain. A ewe in its second year: certainly to the כהן. After that, uncertain. A cow in its third year: certainly to the כהן. After that, uncertain. A donkey is like a cow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that spells out רבי ישמעאל's age guidelines for an animal bought from a non-Jew without knowing whether it already gave birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under these ages the animal is assumed not to have given birth yet, so its next male is a definite בכור. Above these ages it might already have given birth, so the next male is only a ספק בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncertain whether it is a בכור

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
a goat within its first year: the offspring certainly goes to the priest;
from then on, it is uncertain.
a ewe within its second year: certainly to the priest;
from then on, uncertain.
a cow within its third year: certainly to the priest;
from then on, uncertain.
A donkey is like a cow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section by quoting a ברייתא with רבי ישמעאל's full rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Up to a set age for each species, the next male offspring is a definite בכור. After that age it is a ספק.

steps.title: A different age for a donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a donkey's age limit is its fourth year. The ברייתא then marks that this is the end of רבי ישמעאל's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: a donkey in its fourth year. Until here are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a differing view about donkeys and then marks where רבי ישמעאל's statement ends, setting up רבי יהושע's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives a donkey one more year than a cow, so its offspring is still a definite בכור during its fourth year. The closing line, "until here," tells us that what follows is a reaction to רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Until here are the words of

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
a donkey within its fourth year.
Until here are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view about the donkey from the one in step 3 and closes רבי ישמעאל's section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a donkey's offspring is a definite בכור through its fourth year.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: רבי ישמעאל made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says רבי ישמעאל's rule would work only if a live baby were the only thing that exempts the mother from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When these words were said before רבי יהושע, he told them: Go tell רבי ישמעאל, "You erred!" If an animal were exempted only by giving birth to a baby, it would be as you say.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges רבי ישמעאל's age rule and sets up his reason in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's ages assume we only need to know whether the animal gave birth to a baby. רבי יהושע points out that this assumption is too narrow, because other things also exempt the animal.

phrases.english: When these matters were stated before Rabbi Yehoshua,
he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ אִמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: טָעִיתָ!
phrases.english: Go out and say to Rabbi Yishmael: You erred!
If an animal were exempted only by an offspring,
it would be in accordance with your words,

steps.triggerLanguage: צְאוּ אִמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: טָעִיתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the age rule just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's statement that below a certain age the offspring is definitely a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule assumes only a live birth exempts the animal. Since other things exempt it too, even a young animal might already be exempt.

steps.title: Signs of a pregnancy also exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains which physical signs count as a birth: טינוף (murky discharge) in a small animal, שליא (afterbirth) in a large animal, and שפיר or שליא in a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the sign of an offspring in a small animal is a murky discharge. In a large animal it is an afterbirth. In a woman it is a fetal sac or an afterbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע finishes his challenge by explaining what else exempts an animal from בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A murky discharge from a young goat shows there was an early pregnancy, and that alone exempts the next offspring. Such a small sign is easy to miss, so we can never be sure a young animal bought from a non-Jew is still unexempted. That is why רבי ישמעאל's "certainly to the כהן" fails.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע: an animal can be exempted from בכורה by signs of a pregnancy, not only by a live birth. So even a young animal's next offspring is not a definite בכור.
steps.confusionAlert: Even if the animal never gave birth to a live baby, a discharge or afterbirth still counts as its "first birth" and exempts what comes after it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא סִימַן הַוָּולָד בִּבְהֵמָה דַּקָּה — טִינּוּף,
phrases.english: but the sign of the offspring in a small animal is a murky discharge,
and in a large animal, an afterbirth,
and in a woman, a fetal sac or an afterbirth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יהושע's "You erred."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small animal is exempted by a murky discharge, a large animal by an afterbirth, and a woman by a fetal sac or afterbirth.

steps.title: רבי יהושע gives his own view on young animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says a goat that had a טינוף at six months can give birth within its first year, and a ewe that had a טינוף in its first year can give birth within its second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יהושע continues:] But I myself do not say so. Rather: a goat that had a murky discharge at six months can give birth within its first year, and a ewe that had a murky discharge in its first year can give birth within its second year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע finishes his statement. He says even a very young animal may already have had a טינוף, which counts as a birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל assumed that an animal inside the age limit has surely never given birth, so its next baby is surely a בכור. רבי יהושע says a goat can have a טינוף as early as six months. So even a young animal may already be exempt, and its next baby is only a doubtful בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A murky discharge from the womb, which counts as a birth in a small animal

steps.confusionAlert: 'Gives birth within its first year' means a real birth that comes after the טינוף. רבי יהושע's point is that a טינוף does not stop the goat from giving birth later in the same year. So when a young goat gives birth, that birth does not prove there was no earlier, exempting טינוף.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי אֵין אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן, אֶלָּא:
phrases.english: But I myself do not say so; rather:
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע separates his own view from the rule he quoted.

phrases.english: a goat that had a murky discharge at six months old —
gives birth within its (first) year,
a ewe that had a murky discharge in its first year —
gives birth within two (years).

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אֵין אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע's statement, now giving his personal position after defining which signs count as a birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat at six months, or a ewe in its first year, may already have had a טינוף. So young age does not guarantee that the next baby is a בכור.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא rejects age-based rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says he does not use age measurements. If we know the animal gave birth, the כהן gets nothing. If we know it did not, the baby goes to the כהן. If it is a doubt, the owner eats it once it has a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I did not come to use this measure. Rather: whenever it is known that the animal already gave birth, the כהן has nothing here. Whenever it is known that it did not give birth, the baby belongs to the כהן. If it is uncertain, it is eaten by the owners once it has a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view closes the ברייתא. רבי עקיבא throws out the age charts and goes only by what we actually know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע both try to use the mother's age to decide. רבי עקיבא says age proves nothing either way. A doubtful בכור cannot be taken from the owner, but it still has possible קדושה, so it may only be eaten after it gets a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure, here the method of judging by the animal's age
Gave birth for the first time
With its blemish, meaning only after it gets a disqualifying blemish

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a ספק בכור is handled. The owner keeps it, because the כהן cannot prove it is his, but it is treated with caution and eaten only once it is blemished.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי לֹא בָּאתִי לִידֵי מִדָּה זוֹ, אֶלָּא:
phrases.english: I did not come to this measure; rather:
phrases.notes: He rejects judging by age altogether.

phrases.english: any (animal) that is known to have already given birth —
the priest has nothing here,
and any (animal known) not to have given birth —
this (offspring) goes to the priest,
if uncertain — it is eaten in its blemished state by the owners.
phrases.notes: A doubtful בכור stays with the owner but is eaten only after a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲנִי לֹא בָּאתִי לִידֵי מִדָּה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third opinion in the ברייתא, rejecting the age-based approaches of both רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Status depends only on known facts. Known birth means no בכור, known no birth means a בכור for the כהן, and a doubt is eaten by the owner once blemished.

steps.title: What is the real dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע disagree about. It suggests the dispute is whether a טינוף exempts the animal from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע disagree? Shall we say they disagree about whether a murky discharge exempts the animal: רבי ישמעאל holds a murky discharge does not exempt, and רבי יהושע holds a murky discharge does exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts analyzing the ברייתא. It asks for the exact point of the dispute and offers a first guess, which the next step will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל gave age limits and never mentioned טינוף. רבי יהושע focused on טינוף. So the first guess is that רבי ישמעאל simply does not count a טינוף as a birth at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggested answer)
Exempts the mother from the law of בכורה

phrases.english: About what do they disagree —
Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yehoshua?
Shall we say they disagree about whether a murky discharge exempts,
phrases.notes: A suggested answer that the גמרא will reject.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר טִינּוּף אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds a murky discharge does not exempt,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds a murky discharge exempts?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact point of disagreement between רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: Everyone agrees a seen טינוף exempts; the dispute is about an unseen one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the guess. If we saw a טינוף, all agree it exempts. They disagree only about whether we worry that an unseen טינוף happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we see that it had a murky discharge, everyone agrees that a murky discharge exempts. Here they disagree about whether we worry about a murky discharge: רבי ישמעאל holds we do not worry about a murky discharge, and רבי יהושע holds we do worry about a murky discharge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first guess and gives the real dispute: worrying about a טינוף that may have happened without anyone seeing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether a טינוף counts. Both agree a seen טינוף counts. רבי ישמעאל assumes nothing happened, so a young animal's next baby is a sure בכור. רבי יהושע worries it may have happened, so that baby is only a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned about a possibility that was not seen

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two separate questions. One is 'Does a טינוף count?' and everyone says yes. The other is 'Do we suspect one happened unseen?' and that is the only argument.

phrases.english: If we see that it had a murky discharge —

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּטִינּוּף פּוֹטֵר,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that a murky discharge exempts,
and here they disagree about whether we worry about a murky discharge:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְטִינּוּף,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds: we do not worry about a murky discharge,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds: we do worry about a murky discharge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דַּחֲזֵינָא דְּטַינִּוף דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 9 and gives the real dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the two disagree about whether a טינוף exempts at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A seen טינוף clearly exempts according to everyone, so the dispute must be about suspecting an unseen one.

steps.title: But רבא said רבי ישמעאל worries about a minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. רבא said רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר, who worries about a minority. So he should worry about an unseen טינוף too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not worry? But didn't רבא say: it is clear that רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who worries about a minority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim from the last step that רבי ישמעאל ignores a possible unseen טינוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unseen טינוף is an unlikely, minority possibility. רבא had placed רבי ישמעאל with רבי מאיר, who does take minority possibilities into account. So it seems strange that here רבי ישמעאל would ignore one.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) say? (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And he does not worry?
But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: מְחַוַּורְתָּא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: It is clear that Rabbi Yishmael holds like Rabbi Meir,
who worries about the minority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10's claim that רבי ישמעאל does not worry about an unseen טינוף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי ישמעאל holds אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְטִינּוּף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא said רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר and worries about a minority. An unseen טינוף is a minority possibility, so he should worry about it.

steps.title: He worries about a minority only to be strict
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל worries about a minority only when it leads to a חומרא. Here worrying would lead to a קולא, so he does not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he worries, it is for a stringency. For a leniency, he does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting when רבי ישמעאל worries about a minority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worrying about an unseen טינוף would make the baby only a doubtful בכור, which lets the owner keep it. That is a קולא. רבי ישמעאל uses minority worries only to be strict, so here he treats the baby as a sure בכור for the כהן.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a seen טינוף exempts. רבי יהושע worries about an unseen טינוף. רבי ישמעאל does not, because he worries about a minority only when that makes things stricter. Here worrying would be a קולא, since it takes the בכור away from the כהן.

phrases.english: When he worries — it is for a stringency,
for a leniency — he does not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 and keeps the explanation of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting distinction: worrying about a minority applies only when it leads to a stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי ישמעאל worries about a minority, he should worry about an unseen טינוף.
steps.terutzMaskana: He worries about a minority only to be strict. Worrying about a טינוף here would be lenient, since it would turn a sure בכור into a doubtful one, so he ignores it.

steps.title: A different explanation of the argument: can an animal that had a discharge still give birth in its first year?
steps.stepSummary: Second answer. רבי ישמעאל does worry about a minority even when this leads to a קולא. The argument is about nature: can a מטנפת return and give birth within its first year? רבי ישמעאל says no, so a goat that gave birth surely never had a טינוף. רבי יהושע says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this instead: רבי ישמעאל worries about a minority whether it leads to a leniency or to a stringency. Here they argue about an animal that had a discharge: can it go back and give birth within its first year? רבי ישמעאל holds that an animal that had a discharge cannot go back and give birth within its first year. So since this animal gave birth, it certainly did not have a discharge. רבי יהושע holds that an animal that had a discharge can go back and give birth within its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to answer the challenge from רבא (step 11). It moves the argument away from 'worrying about a minority' and onto a question of animal biology.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 we said רבי ישמעאל ignores a minority when that leads to a קולא. Now the גמרא says he may worry either way. He simply holds that a טינוף and a birth cannot both happen in the first year. Once the goat gave birth within its year, an earlier טינוף is impossible, so there is nothing left to worry about. רבי יהושע holds that both can happen, so he still has a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': introduces a second, alternative answer
He is concerned / takes the possibility into account
An animal that expelled a murky discharge (טינוף), which can count as a first birth and exempt later offspring from בכורה
Goes back (becomes fertile again) and gives birth
Within its first year of life

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rejection of step 12. It is a second, alternative answer (ואיבעית אימא). Both answers stand as possible ways to explain רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
phrases.notes: Signals an alternative answer to the challenge of step 11.

phrases.english: whether for a leniency or for a stringency, he is concerned (about a minority),
phrases.notes: Reverses the assumption of step 12.

phrases.english: and here, regarding an animal that discharges and returns
and gives birth within its first year, they disagree.
phrases.notes: The new point of argument: a fact of nature.

phrases.english: For רבי ישמעאל holds:
an animal that discharges does not return
and give birth within its first year,
and this one, since it gave birth,
certainly did not discharge.
phrases.notes: So the doubt disappears, and the offspring is a definite בכור.

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע holds:
an animal that discharges does return and give birth within its first year.
phrases.notes: So a birth does not prove there was no earlier טינוף, and the doubt remains.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בֵּין לְקוּלָּא בֵּין לְחוּמְרָא חָיֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 11, in place of the answer in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point of dispute (from legal presumption to biological fact)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל, who follows רבי מאיר, should worry about an unseen טינוף, and the only way out was to limit that worry to חומרא cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל worries in all cases. But by his view of nature, a goat that gave birth in its first year could not have had a טינוף, so there is nothing to worry about.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's own view on when an animal that had a discharge can give birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the ברייתא. רבי יהושע says he personally does not hold like the tradition he quoted. A goat that had a טינוף at six months can give birth within its first year. A ewe that had a טינוף in its first year can give birth within its second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I do not say so. Rather, a goat that had a discharge at six months old can give birth within its first year. A ewe that had a discharge in its first year can give birth within its second year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא, where רבי יהושע gives his own opinion, separate from the tradition he received. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהושע reported a tradition (the view of the חכמים). Now he says 'I do not say so' and gives his own rule. Both views seem to agree that an animal that had a טינוף can still give birth within a year. That is exactly why the גמרא will ask what the difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But I do not say so': the speaker separates his own view from what he quoted

phrases.english: But I do not say so;
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע speaking, in contrast to the tradition he cited.

phrases.english: rather, a goat that discharged at six months old
gives birth within its first year;
a ewe that discharged in its first year
gives birth within two (years).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes רבי יהושע's line from the ברייתא (first given in step 7) to open a new question about it, now that step 13 has finished explaining his dispute with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat that had a טינוף at six months can still give birth within its first year. A ewe that had a טינוף in its first year can give birth within its second year.

steps.title: What is the difference between his tradition and his own reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: Both the tradition and רבי יהושע's own view allow an animal that had a טינוף to give birth within the year. So the גמרא asks what practical difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between his tradition and his own reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: the two views sound the same, so where do they actually lead to different results? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions say a טינוף does not stop a birth within the year. If they never produce a different result, רבי יהושע's 'I do not say so' would mean nothing. The גמרא therefore looks for the specific case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is there between': what practical difference exists between two views
His received tradition (what he learned from his teachers)

phrases.english: What (difference) is there
between his tradition and his reasoning?
phrases.notes: The tradition (the חכמים's view he reported) versus his own view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical difference between the tradition and the personal view just quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case do רבי יהושע's received tradition and his own reasoning give different rulings?

steps.title: The difference: a goat that discharged at the end of six months, and זעירי's thirty-day rule
steps.stepSummary: They differ about a goat that had a טינוף at the end of six months and then gave birth by the end of its first year. The difference depends on זעירי's rule that a real טינוף is followed by at least thirty days without pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is when the goat had a discharge at the end of six months. And the difference between them is about זעירי's rule, for זעירי said: a discharge is not less than thirty days (a real discharge blocks pregnancy for at least thirty days).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It names the exact case where the two views split and the rule they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goat's pregnancy lasts five months. If it had a טינוף at the end of month six and gave birth by month twelve, it must have become pregnant within about a month of the טינוף. זעירי says a real טינוף blocks pregnancy for at least thirty days. So if the goat got pregnant sooner, the 'טינוף' was not a real one and does not exempt the animal from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of six months
There is a difference between them (in this point)
An אמורא whose rule on טינוף is quoted here

phrases.english: Where it discharged at the end of six (months),
phrases.notes: Then it gave birth before the end of its first year, so it became pregnant within about a month.

phrases.english: and the difference between them is (the rule) of זעירי,
for זעירי said:
there is no discharge (that counts) of less than thirty days.
phrases.notes: A real, exempting טינוף means no new pregnancy for at least thirty days. Pregnancy sooner shows it was not a real טינוף.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁטִּינְּפָה בְּסוֹף שִׁשָּׁה, וְאִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דִּזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by naming the case and the rule in dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ about a goat that had a טינוף at the end of six months and gave birth within its year. The question is whether זעירי's thirty-day rule applies.

steps.title: The tradition accepts זעירי's rule; רבי יהושע's own reasoning does not
steps.stepSummary: The tradition (גמריה) accepts זעירי's rule, so this goat's טינוף does not exempt it and the offspring is a בכור. רבי יהושע's own reasoning (סבריה) rejects זעירי's rule, so the טינוף still exempts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to his tradition, it holds like זעירי. According to his own reasoning, it does not hold like זעירי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by saying which side holds like זעירי and which does not. The next step offers a second, alternative answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the tradition, the goat got pregnant within thirty days, so its 'טינוף' was not real and the next offspring is a בכור. Under רבי יהושע's own view, a real טינוף can be followed quickly by pregnancy. So the טינוף still counts and exempts the later offspring from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold / does not accept

steps.whatToRemember: Tradition (גמריה) holds like זעירי: a real טינוף blocks pregnancy for thirty days, so a quick pregnancy means no exemption. Reasoning (סבריה) does not hold like זעירי: the טינוף still exempts even if pregnancy came quickly.

phrases.english: According to his tradition, he holds (the rule) of זעירי;
phrases.notes: So the goat is not exempt, and its offspring is a בכור.

phrases.english: according to his reasoning, he does not hold (the rule) of זעירי.
phrases.notes: So the טינוף exempts the animal even though it became pregnant within a month.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִגְמָרֵיהּ — אִית לֵיהּ דִּזְעֵירִי, לִסְבָרֵיהּ — לֵית לֵיהּ דִּזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 16 by saying which side accepts זעירי's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical difference between רבי יהושע's tradition and his own reasoning is whether זעירי's thirty-day rule is accepted. The tradition accepts it, and his reasoning rejects it.

steps.title: Everyone accepts זעירי; the dispute is about birth after incomplete months
steps.stepSummary: An alternative answer to the question from step 15. Both the tradition and רבי יהושע accept זעירי's thirty-day rule. Their real disagreement is whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months of pregnancy (יולדת למקוטעין).
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: everyone accepts זעירי's rule. Here they disagree about whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question 'what is the difference between the tradition and רבי יהושע?' This time it keeps זעירי's rule for both sides and finds a different point of disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the case of the goat (טינוף at the end of six months, then birth by the end of its first year) depended on accepting or rejecting זעירי. Now both sides agree that thirty days must pass with no pregnancy after the טינוף. That leaves only a tight window for the pregnancy to finish within the year, so the question becomes whether a pregnancy can end short of its full months (למקוטעין).

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say' – introduces an alternative answer
Everyone, meaning both sides of the dispute
Gives birth after incomplete (partial) months, i.e., before the full term

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the difference between the tradition and רבי יהושע. (1) They disagree about זעירי's thirty-day rule. (2) Both accept זעירי, and they disagree about whether an animal gives birth למקוטעין.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this answer rejects זעירי. It does the opposite: it says BOTH sides accept זעירי. What changed is the reason for the dispute, not the status of זעירי's rule.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
phrases.notes: Signals an alternative answer to the question from step 15.

phrases.english: that everyone accepts the rule of Ze'eiri,
phrases.notes: Both the tradition and רבי יהושע agree that a real טינוף is followed by thirty days without pregnancy.

phrases.english: and here, they disagree about whether an animal gives birth after incomplete months.
phrases.notes: The case is the goat with a טינוף at the end of six months that gave birth within its first year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation that replaces the זעירי-based difference from steps 16-17. Here זעירי is accepted by both sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between the tradition (גמריה) and רבי יהושע's own view (סבריה)? (question from step 15)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both accept זעירי. They differ over a goat with a טינוף at the end of six months that gave birth within the year. The question is whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months (למקוטעין).
